clips.title: What Is a Workflow in Temporal? A Clear Explanation
clips.why: Temporal's own short definition of its kind of workflow, so the word has a clear first meaning before we add the second one.
look: A Temporal workflow is durable: a failure in the middle does not lose the steps already done.
It runs as code you write, on workers you run. In our platform that is the orchestrator, outside every VM.
Keep this meaning apart from a Claude Code dynamic workflow, which is a script inside one agent session.
clips.after: ticketToPr and the parallel attempts are this kind of workflow; nova-research and nova-review-panel are the other kind.

clips.title: Claude Code Worktrees in 7 Minutes
clips.why: On a laptop, writers in parallel each get their own copy of the repo with git worktrees. It is the same rule we follow with separate VMs.
look: Why agents benefit: each one edits its own copy, so their changes never mix.
The demo of two parallel edits with no conflicts. In the story, the shared checkout had exactly those conflicts.
Where the copies live and what they share. Our attempts share nothing but the approved plan and the locked checks.
clips.after: A worktree isolates files on one machine; our attempts isolate the whole machine, so a dead VM or a broken test in one attempt cannot touch another.

clips.title: Orca Coding Agents: When Parallel Agents Beat One Stronger Run
clips.why: A sober look at when racing several coding agents pays: isolation, failures that are correlated, and the cost of reviewing the results.
look: Worktree isolation is the starting condition, as for our attempts.
Correlated failures: attempts from the same model and plan often fail the same way, which is why we measure before keeping the feature.
The review bill: several results cost review time. We avoid it by letting tests and a judge pick, so people review only one PR.
clips.after: That is why parallel attempts are a stretch goal for hard tickets only, kept only if the bench shows enough gain for the extra VMs.

practice.q: Which of these is a dynamic workflow, not a Temporal workflow?

options.why: That is Nova's Temporal workflow on the orchestrator, one per ticket.
A saved script that Claude Code runs inside the reviewer's session in the VM.
A Temporal child workflow started by ticketToPr for one attempt.

practice.q: Finish the parent so one failed attempt cannot fail the whole ticket.
practice.hint: The Promise method that waits for every promise, whatever happens to each one.
practice.why: Promise.all rejects as soon as one attempt fails, and the surviving attempts' work is lost with it.

practice.q: Name the second attempt of RH-1234's run as a child workflow ID.
practice.hint: The parent's ID, a colon, then the attempt.
practice.why: Every run is named after the thing it works on. The attempt number makes each child unique inside the ticket's run.

practice.q: Why is the review panel started from the read-only reviewer session, not from Nova's own session?

options.text: Because the reviewer session is cheaper
options.why: The models are the same. The reason is permissions.

options.text: Because a workflow's agents use their session's permissions, so they cannot edit anything
options.why: Started from a session with only Read, Grep, Glob and Workflow, no lens or skeptic can change a file.

options.text: Because Nova's session cannot run workflows
options.why: It can; Workflow is in Nova's allowedTools. It is simply the wrong place for reviewers.

practice.q: Put a run with parallel attempts in order.
items: The approved plan marks the ticket hard
ticketToPr starts two or three buildAttempt children, each claiming a slot, a full VM and its own branch
Attempts that fail a locked check or other tests are dropped
A judge compares the surviving diffs and check results and picks one
Only the winner goes on to self-review and the PR; the others' VMs are released
practice.why: Isolated writers first, then the tests filter, then the judge picks, and one change ships.
